A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FlexOlmo study and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–D. Renumbered tables and relocated material can be matched without material gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, ablations, routing and data-extraction analyses in Section 5, plus Reddit preprocessing experiments in Appendix B.1.

after.justification: v4 retains those original empirical results and adds weighted model-soup and router-initialization comparisons in Tables 1 and 3.

M1.justification: The coordinated expert training, frozen public anchor, domain-informed router, negative bias and optional proxy-data router tuning remain unchanged. GRIT initialization already appears in v1; the new comparison tests an alternative initialization without revising the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Public Mix, seven domain datasets and downstream task coverage. The added comparisons use existing benchmarks; the appendix Reddit preprocessing experiment is also retained.

E2.justification: v4 Table 1 adds weighted model soup. The original uniform model soup remains as 'Model soup (average)', and BTM, both prompt-based routers, BTX and unrestricted MoE comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New Table 3 introduces public-model hidden-state initialization as an experimental control against GRIT initialization. Existing training budgets, metrics, sample counts and generation/extraction protocols remain unchanged. The revised inference-FLOP figure does not establish a changed experimental budget or a rerun.

E4.justification: v4 adds an ablation testing GRIT router initialization against public-model hidden states, extending v1's component-removal ablations. Existing coordination, bias, expert-count, routing, opt-out, extraction and appendix Reddit analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five news/poem completions per prompt and ten extraction attempts per prefix. Neither adds training-run counts, seed reporting, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds weighted-soup results, averaging 42.2. New Table 3 adds public-initialization results averaging 43.5 alongside reused GRIT results averaging 46.7. The scaling table changes reported inference FLOPs from 3x to 2.5x (v1 Table 3; v4 Table 4), while retaining all its benchmark scores. Other existing results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3's mathematical formulation, Appendix A.1's ensemble equations and Appendix D's classification definitions and anchor/bias reasoning are unchanged. No new theorem, proof or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about independent distributed training, flexible data inclusion/exclusion and model-merging advantages, including the reported 41% and 10.1% relative improvements.

C2.justification: Interpretations of expert coordination, specialization, routing and opt-out behavior remain unchanged, as do the data-leakage qualifications and differential-privacy recommendation. The added initialization statement reports an empirical comparison without introducing a new mechanism explanation or applicability boundary.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 documents the new weighted-soup implementation: averaging weights come from a softmax over each model's test-input log likelihood. Existing hardware, training hyperparameters, preprocessing instructions, appendix implementation details and resource links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related-work and router-motivation coverage expands to include asynchronous federated learning, DEMix, BAM!, ModuleFormer, AdapterSwap, Nexus and additional model-collaboration work. The Akhlaghi–Sukhov knowledge-fusion reference is removed. These additions refine the existing positioning rather than substantially redefine it.

P1.justification: Localized prose revisions expand related work, describe weighted model soup and discuss the added initialization comparison. The overall narrative, section organization and appendix content remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 adds initialization Table 3 and a weighted-soup row to Table 1. Existing figures shift with the text reflow, and later tables are renumbered. The existing figure images are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's uniform-soup comparison and existing initialization ablations, v4 adds a stronger weighted-soup comparator and a targeted public-model initialization control. These additions modestly strengthen comparative validation and support the GRIT design choice; expanded related work improves context. The core method, benchmark coverage, principal results and privacy limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
